paper.title: Learning to Commit: Generating Organic Pull Requests via Online Repository Memory
paper.central_claim: Oracle-supervised contrastive reflection on historical commits builds persistent repository skills that improve organicity and correctness of future PR generation.

provenance.notes: Configured sonnet -> gpt-6.1-sol; no independent provider receipt/session identifier exposed; not probed. Blind: only own a1 directory accessed.

sections_read: end of HTML; no appendix supplied in source

evidence.quote: the agent updates the skill document through explicit CRUD operations
evidence.support_explanation: Oracle contrast produces create/revise/deprecate updates to reusable text.
Oracle expert diffs are revealed after blind historical attempts, not a label-free autonomous evaluator.

evidence.quote: and the full accumulated skill document
evidence.support_explanation: The retained document is read on future solve tasks; this is not just within-answer correction.

evidence.quote: 24 historical learning commits and 7 genuinely future, held-out test tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: One private repository and seven temporal test tasks define the empirical scope.

evidence.quote: both powered by Claude Opus 4.6 with identical tool-use capabilities.
evidence.support_explanation: Store-off comparison uses the same base and tools, with four construction regimes.
Seq-all improves file IoU; steps 56.8 vs 71.9 and line deviation .69 vs 1.59 are Table 2, not functional pass rates.

evidence.quote: while the baseline retains a slight edge on Q1 (scope alignment) and Q4 (code style).
evidence.support_explanation: Organicity gains are dimension-specific and do not establish better code style.

evidence.quote: we run evaluations with two independent judge models and report agreement rates.
evidence.support_explanation: Pairwise LLM judgments measure oracle similarity rather than real maintainer acceptance; no numeric agreement table is supplied.

evidence.quote: an LLM synthesises an issue-style natural-language query from the commit message and diff.
evidence.support_explanation: Temporal split does not independently audit implementation hints in oracle-derived issues or guarantee pretraining non-overlap.

evidence.quote: relying on LLMs as evaluators inherently introduces potential biases and inaccuracies
evidence.support_explanation: Authors acknowledge judge limitations and single-repository generalization remains future work.
Closest continual-memory neighbor is described by the paper, not independently read.

evidence.quote: Conversely, the largest negative effect occurs on a training-step guard logic fix
evidence.support_explanation: A negative example is disclosed, but no repeat-run uncertainty is reported.

signatures.object: Persistent repository skill document, initialized empty
signatures.information: Historical parent snapshots and synthetic issues; expert diff hidden during attempt then revealed; future oracle excluded from skill building
signatures.operation: Blind patch -> contrast with expert diff -> CRUD skill edits
signatures.conditions: Reviewed historical commits and recurring repository conventions
signatures.selection_rule: Curator creates/revises/deprecates entries against oracle evidence; no measured marginal utility acceptance gate
signatures.selection_data: 24 past commits; category-specific or full curriculum
signatures.persistence: Skill document across onboarding commits; sequential fusion or parallel extraction with pairwise merge
signatures.later_use: Full frozen accumulated document supplied for seven later tasks
signatures.claimed_effect: Higher future patch organicity/localization and less redundant code
signatures.failure_boundary: Private single repo; negative seq-bycat and code-style effects; no regression-gated curation

gap.author_gap: Snapshot-only and unsupervised continual agents miss expert repository change patterns and accumulate self-reflection errors.
gap.checked_gap: Specific missing expert-supervised onboarding is coherent; historical memory and continual SWE are already acknowledged, so no broad novelty claim is verified.

claims.text: Onboarding skills improve organicity on future PRs
claims.setting: One private RL training repository; Opus 4.6
claims.baseline/control: Same model/tools without skill document; four construction regimes
claims.selection_vs_test: 24 historical commits build skills; 7 later commits test; no future-label skill update claimed
claims.result/denominator: 7 tasks each regime; seq-all file IoU .80/.61, steps 56.8/71.9, line deviation .69/1.59; judges 55/58% aggregate wins
claims.allowed_conclusion: Retained guidance improves selected proxy outcomes in this small time-split pilot.

claims.text: Organically aligned and functionally correct PRs / zero leakage
claims.setting: Oracle-relative metrics and synthetic task descriptions
claims.baseline/control: Two LLM judges plus deterministic file/size metrics
claims.selection_vs_test: Temporal split controls memory construction leakage, not every oracle-derived query or pretraining channel
claims.result/denominator: par-bycat style skill wins 27%, base 38%, ties 36%; no functional pass or maintainer-acceptance denominator
claims.allowed_conclusion: No demonstrated functional-correctness or actual merge-rate gain; zero-data-leakage is stronger than checked protocol.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported same-repository temporal store-on/off comparison supports retained guidance improving localization/redundancy on seven tasks in some regimes; not functional correctness, real merge acceptance or broadly superior code style.
unresolved: No functional test-pass evaluation reported despite correctness framing
No source-code execution or replication performed
